metadata.title: झारखंड में पेसा 1996 के नियमों पर घमासान | Fight Over Rules Must Not Delay PESA 1996 In Jharkhand
metadata.description:
The ongoing debate over the draft rules of the PESA (Panchayats Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996, has stirred intense discussions in Jharkhand, with tribal organisations and activists voicing strong opposition. Many believe that the draft rules undermine the core spirit of PESA, which aims to empower Gram Sabhas and protect the rights of tribals in scheduled areas. Critics argue that the proposed rules dilute tribal autonomy by centralising decision-making powers with the government.

However, noted activist Sudhir Pal has taken a different stand, defending the draft rules as a practical step toward implementing PESA in Jharkhand. In an exclusive interview with Main Bhi Bharat, Pal acknowledged the shortcomings in the draft but argued that they represent the best possible framework under the current circumstances. He emphasised that having rules, even if imperfect, is better than the continued absence of PESA implementation in the state. According to Pal, the draft rules provide a foundation for tribal governance, ensuring that Gram Sabhas will have a significant say in local matters, including land, resources, and cultural preservation.

While his views have sparked debate within the tribal community, Pal insists that constructive dialogue is essential to refine the rules further and achieve true tribal self-governance as envisioned in PESA.
